reasons: No test is visible for this store.
A failed calculation leaves old results on screen.
Loading defaults discards user edits without asking.
Several places use the loose any type, so some mistakes are not caught.

terms.meaning: A small library that keeps shared app data in one place that any screen can read.
One saved calculation run, stored on the backend under an id.
The part of the store library that saves some data in the browser so it survives a refresh.
The helper that sends requests from the app to the backend and returns the replies.
A named function that changes the stored data, such as calculate or reset.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the store
sections.what: Explains what the file is for and brings in the store library, the browser-saving helper, the shared data types, and the API client that talks to the backend.
sections.why: Likely reason: the store is the single place where screens read and change model data.

sections.name: ModelState
sections.title: List of stored data and actions
sections.what: Lists every piece of shared data the store holds, such as the session, inputs, outputs, research, lecture steps, errors, and loading flags. It also lists the actions screens can call.
sections.why: Likely reason: writing the shape in one place helps the screens and the store agree on the same names.
sections.watch_out: A field added here must also get a starting value below, or the type check will complain.

sections.name: normalizeInputs
sections.title: Cleaning up partly typed numbers
sections.what: Before inputs go to the backend, replaces any number field the user left blank or half-typed (an empty box, a lone minus sign, or a lone dot) with its default value. The backend therefore receives only real numbers.
sections.why: The code comment says the backend should only ever receive numbers.
sections.watch_out: If defaults have not loaded yet, a blank field is sent with no value, which the backend may reject.

sections.name: useModelStore (part 1)
sections.title: Starting values, creating and loading sessions
sections.what: Sets the empty starting values and wraps the store in the browser-saving helper. Creating a session sends the current inputs to the backend. Loading a session copies its saved inputs, outputs, research, lecture steps, checks, and warnings into the store.
sections.why: Likely reason: sessions let the backend keep a record of each run so it can be reopened or exported later.
sections.watch_out: When a call fails, the store records the message and then throws the error again, so every caller must catch it.

sections.name: useModelStore (part 2)
sections.title: Setting inputs and running the calculation
sections.what: Stores new inputs and changes one input at a time. Running the calculation sends the cleaned inputs with a session id, then saves the returned outputs, research, lecture steps, checks, and warnings. If the backend reports failure, it keeps the error and the check list.
sections.why: Likely reason: a session id is made in the browser if none exists, because the code comment says the backend only keeps a session when given an id.
sections.watch_out: When a calculation fails, the old outputs stay on screen next to the new error, so the user may read stale numbers.

sections.name: useModelStore (part 3)
sections.title: Excel export and small view switches
sections.what: Downloads the current session as an Excel file named with the first eight characters of the session id. It also holds small switches: which lecture step is showing, which schematic part is active, and whether the lecture and research panels are visible.
sections.why: Likely reason: a downloaded file is triggered through a temporary link, which the code creates and removes.
sections.watch_out: Export needs a session id, so pressing it before the first calculation will show an error.

sections.name: useModelStore (part 4)
sections.title: Reset, loading defaults, and what gets saved
sections.what: Clears the working data back to empty (reset). Loads the default inputs from the backend and sets them as the current inputs. Also defines what is saved in the browser: the session id, the inputs, and the two panel switches.
sections.why: Likely reason: saving only a few fields keeps browser storage small and lets the backend resend larger results when needed.
sections.watch_out: Loading defaults overwrites every input the user has typed, with no confirmation.

summary: The shared memory of the frontend: it holds the model's inputs, results, and session, and provides the actions screens use to change them and talk to the backend.
purpose: Keeps one copy of the data the app shows so the screens stay in agreement.
why: Likely reason: one shared store avoids passing the same data through many layers of components.
how: 1. Start with empty values and settings. 2. When the app loads, fetch default inputs or open a saved session. 3. When the user edits, update the inputs locally. 4. When a calculation runs, clean the inputs, send them with a session id, and store the results or the error. 5. Export downloads the Excel file. 6. Some values are saved in the browser so they survive a page refresh.
inputs: Actions called by screens: create or load a session, update inputs, calculate with optional lecture and research flags, export, load defaults, reset, and small toggles. It also reads replies from the backend client.
outputs: Stored values the screens read: outputs, research, lecture steps, validation results, warnings, errors, and loading flags. It also triggers an Excel file download.
risks: Loading defaults overwrites the user's edits with no warning. A failed calculation keeps the old outputs on screen. Reset does not clear the export flag or the default inputs. Callers must catch the errors the actions rethrow. Saved inputs come back after a refresh, so an old input can reappear.
debug: If numbers look stale, check whether a calculation failed and left old outputs in place. If inputs change unexpectedly, look for a call to load defaults. If export fails, check that a session id exists. If a value is sent as missing, check whether defaults were loaded. Saved browser data sits under the key solar-model-storage and can be cleared in browser developer tools.
